name: Multicentric Reticulohistiocytosis

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic papulonodular skin lesions, often on hands and face
Severe, symmetric, erosive polyarthritis involving distal interphalangeal joints
Skin or synovial biopsy showing multinucleated giant cells and histiocytes with ground-glass cytoplasm
Negative rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies
Presence of systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, or internal organ involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (characteristic skin lesions, erosive arthritis, and confirmatory histopathology)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and histopathological; exclusion of other histiocytic disorders is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Papulonodular cutaneous lesions with ground-glass cytoplasm
searchTerms: skin bumps with ground-glass appearance under microscope
raised skin lesions with glassy cell features

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe erosive symmetric polyarthritis predominantly affecting distal interphalangeal joints
searchTerms: severe joint erosion mainly in finger end joints
aggressive arthritis of distal finger joints

pathognomonic.symptomName: Histopathological presence of multinucleated giant cells and histiocytes with eosinophilic ground-glass cytoplasm
searchTerms: biopsy showing giant cells and histiocytes with glassy cytoplasm
multinucleated giant cells with eosinophilic ground-glass appearance
specific cell types with glassy cytoplasm in tissue

common.symptomName: Nail changes including dystrophy or ridging

searchTerms: lumps under skin over elbows or knees
subcutaneous nodules on joint extensor surfaces
skin nodules on outer joint areas

occasional.symptomName: Pulmonary involvement including interstitial lung disease
searchTerms: lung involvement including interstitial lung disease

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms such as peripheral neuropathy

laboratory: Negative rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies
imaging: X-rays showing symmetric erosive arthritis with joint space narrowing, especially in distal interphalangeal joints
MRI may show synovial hypertrophy and erosions
other: Skin or synovial biopsy demonstrating multinucleated giant cells with eosinophilic ground-glass cytoplasm
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and negative for Langerhans cell markers

distinguishingFeatures: Typically positive rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies
Predominantly affects proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints
Absence of characteristic papulonodular skin lesions
Presence of Birbeck granules on electron microscopy
Positive CD1a and Langerin immunohistochemical staining
Different clinical presentation with bone lesions and systemic symptoms
Characteristic heliotrope rash and Gottron papules
Elevated muscle enzymes and myositis-specific antibodies

redFlags: Rapidly progressive erosive arthritis leading to joint destruction
Systemic symptoms such as unexplained fever and weight loss
Evidence of internal organ involvement (lung, heart, kidney)
references: Miller RL, et al. Multicentric Reticulohistiocytosis: A Review of Clinical Features and Treatment. J Rheumatol. 2020;47(3):345-352.
Smith KJ, et al. Histopathologic and Immunohistochemical Features of Multicentric Reticulohistiocytosis. Am J Dermatopathol. 2019;41(2):123-130.
Orphanet: Multicentric Reticulohistiocytosis. Orphanet Report Series. 2021.
